title: Fasten a bracelet on a wrist form
instruction: Fasten the bracelet around the wrist form, then let go and leave it secure.
context: Helping someone fasten small jewellery requires holding a flexible band, aligning its clasp and closing it without dropping either end. This trial uses a rigid wrist form.
setup: A 220 mm long, 54 mm diameter rigid silicone wrist form is fixed horizontally on two 25 x 80 x 25 mm rigid supports. Below it, a 195 mm exposed length, 10 x 2 mm leather bracelet has two 10 x 12 x 7 mm metal clasp housings, initially 154 mm apart, with the leather ends folded back. The male end has a 3 mm exposed, 2.2 mm square pin beyond a 3 mm long, 5 mm square stop collar. The female has a 4 mm square bore and a spring detent at 2.5 mm entry. Each housing sits freely on a fixed 6 x 10 x 10 mm acrylic rest. Both hands start open. CLASP.md specifies the equivalent mechanism and fixed reset shown in the setup image.
scoring: 1.0 if the clasp is closed, the intact bracelet surrounds the wrist form within 5 cm of its midpoint, and both hands have released it for three seconds. 0.5 if it is closed around the form but still held. 0.25 if the pin has entered the socket by at least 1 mm but has not caught. Otherwise 0. A broken, overstretched or off-wrist bracelet scores 0. Inspect the clasp and released bracelet with photographs and a ruler.
fidelity: Native PhysX arms, clasp bodies, hollow socket and jointed leather panels. Finger friction grips both ends; neither is attached to a hand. A reduced insertion-gated catch represents the specified internal leaf springs and grooved pin, with axial twist; the solid collar stops entry at 3 mm. Demo uses measured clasp poses; Dream uses ordinary cameras/joints. Bending, friction and the 30 N break setting are uncalibrated. Fabrication is specified, not physically tested.
reset_notes: Open the clasp, fold the leather ends back so it leaves the rear of each housing, and restore the photographed band and wrist-form layout. Let it settle and open both hands. Nothing is consumed.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0; scripted demo: 1.0. Dream completed across 21 server sessions with expiry recovery.
